source_text: Τούτοις καὶ Εὐσέβιος ὑπέγραψε Ῥωμαϊστὶ, ὧν ἡ ἑρμηνεία· Ἐγὼ Εὐσέβιος ἐπίσκοπος κατὰ τὴν ἀκρίβειαν ὑμῶν τὴν παρ' ἑκατέρων τῶν μερῶν ὁμολογηθεῖσαν ἀλλήλοις συντιθεμένων περὶ τῶν ὑποστάσεων, καὶ αὐτὸς συγκατεθέμην· οὐ μὴν ἀλλὰ καὶ περὶ τῆς σαρκώσεως τοῦ Σωτῆρος ἡμῶν, ὅτι ὁ τοῦ Θεοῦ Υἱὸς, καὶ ἄνθρωπος γέγονεν, ἀναλαβὼν πάντα ἄνευ ἁμαρτίας, οἷος ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνέστηκε, κατὰ τὸ τῆς ἐπιστολῆς ὕφος ἐπιστωσάμην. Καὶ ἐπειδὴ ἔξωθεν λέγεται τὸ τῆς Σαρδικῆς πιττάκιον ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν δοκεῖν ἐκτίθεσθαι, καὶ ἐγὼ συγκατατίθεμαι, ἵνα μὴ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστις διὰ τούτου ἐκκλείεσθαι δόξῃ, μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον. Ἐῤῥῶσθαι ὑμᾶς ἐν Κυρίῳ εὔχομαι. Ἐγὼ Ἀστέριος συνευδοκῶ τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις, καὶ ἐῤῥῶσθαι ὑμᾶς ἐν Κυρίῳ εὔχομαι. Καὶ μετὰ τὸ ἀποσταλῆναι ἀπὸ Ἀλεξανδρείας τὸν τόμον τοῦτον, οὕτω παρὰ τῶν προειρημένων ὑπογεγραμμένον, μετὰ ταῦτα καὶ αὐτοὶ ὑπέγραψαν· Ἐγὼ Παυλῖνος οὕτω φρονῶ, καθὼς παρέλαβον παρὰ τῶν Πατέρων, Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Πατέρα τέλειον καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Υἱὸν τέλειον, καὶ ὑφεστηκὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τέλειον. Διὸ καὶ ἀποδέχομαι τὴν προγεγραμμένην ἑρμηνείαν περὶ τῶν τριῶν ὑποστάσεων, καὶ τῆς μιᾶς ὑποστάσεως, ἤτοι οὐσίας, καὶ τοὺς φρονοῦντας οὕτως. Εὐσεβὲς γάρ ἐστι φρονεῖν καὶ ὁμολογεῖν τὴν ἁγίαν Τριάδα ἐν μιᾷ θεότητι. Καὶ περὶ τῆς ἐνανθρωπήσεως δὲ τῆς δι' ἡμᾶς γενομένης τοῦ Λόγου τοῦ Πατρὸς οὕτω φρονῶ, καθὼς γέγραπται, ὅτι, κατὰ τὸν Ἰωάννην, ὁ Λόγος σὰρξ ἐγένετο· οὐ κατὰ τοὺς ἀσεβεστάτους τοὺς λέγοντας μεταβολὴν αὐτὸν πεπονθέναι, ἀλλ' ὅτι ἄνθρωπος δι' ἡμᾶς γέγονεν, ἐκ τῆς ἁγίας Παρθένου Μαρίας καὶ ἁγίου Πνεύματος γεννηθείς. Οὔτε γὰρ ἄψυχον, οὔτε ἀναίσθητον, οὔτε ἀνόητον σῶμα εἶχεν ὁ Σωτήρ· οὔτε γὰρ οἷόν τ' ἦν, τοῦ Κυρίου ἀνθρώπου δι' ἡμᾶς γενομένου, ἀνόητον εἶναι αὐτοῦ τὸ σῶμα. Ὅθεν ἀναθεματίζω τοὺς τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ ὁμολογηθεῖσαν πίστιν ἀθετοῦντας, καὶ μὴ λέγοντας ἐκ τῆς οὐσίας τοῦ Πατρὸς, καὶ ὁμοούσιον εἶναι τὸν Υἱὸν τῷ Πατρί. Ἀναθεματίζω δὲ τοὺς λέγοντας τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον κτίσμα δι' Υἱοῦ γεγονός. Ἔτι δὲ ἀναθεματίζω Σαβελλίου καὶ Φωτεινοῦ, καὶ πᾶσαν αἵρεσιν, στοιχῶν τῇ πίστει τῇ κατὰ Νίκαιαν, καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις. Ἐῤῥῶσθαι ὑμᾶς εὔχομαι ἐγὼ Καρτέριος.
orientation: After the main letter, Eusebius, Asterius, Paulinus, and Carterius each add their own subscription or confession, with Paulinus and Carterius signing after the tome was sent from Alexandria.
pass_a_gloss: To these things Eusebius also subscribed in Latin, of which the translation is: I Eusebius, bishop, according to the exactness of you, the confession agreed to one another by both parties as they composed together concerning the persons, I myself also assented. Not only but also concerning the incarnation of our Savior, that the Son of God also became man, taking up all things without sin, such as our old man was constituted, according to the style of the letter I affirmed. And since from outside the document of Sardica is spoken of for the sake of not seeming to set forth beyond the faith in Nicaea, I also assent, so that the faith in Nicaea may not seem to be shut out through this, nor is it to be brought forward. I pray that you may be well in the Lord. I Asterius agree with the things written above, and I pray that you may be well in the Lord. And after this tome was sent from Alexandria, thus subscribed by the aforementioned, after these things they themselves also subscribed: I Paulinus think thus, just as I received from the Fathers, the Father being and existing perfect, and the Son existing perfect, and the Holy Spirit existing perfect. Therefore I also accept the interpretation written above concerning the three persons, and the one person, or being, and those who think thus. For it is pious to think and confess the holy Trinity in one divinity. And concerning the incarnation of the Word of the Father which happened for us, I think thus, just as it is written, that, according to John, the Word became flesh; not according to the most impious ones who say that he suffered change, but that he became man for us, born from the holy Virgin Mary and the Holy Spirit. For neither did the Savior have a soul-less, nor unfeeling, nor mindless body; for neither was it possible, since the Lord became man for us, that his body be mindless. Therefore I condemn those who reject the faith confessed in Nicaea, and who do not say that the Son is from the being of the Father and same in being with the Father. And I condemn those who say that the Holy Spirit is a creature made through the Son. And further I condemn Sabellius and Photinus, and every heresy, following the faith according to Nicaea, and all the things written above. I Carterius pray that you may be well in the Lord.

choices.english: according to the exactness of you
choices.why: ἀκρίβεια means precision or exactness, referring to the careful investigation of the parties, not a statement; the genitive ὑμῶν is possessive.
rejected: according to the exact statement of you

choices.english: taking up all things without sin
choices.why: ἀναλαβών means taking up; πάντα is the object of taking up, meaning complete human nature; ἄνευ ἁμαρτίας modifies what was taken, not the manner of taking.
rejected: taking on all things without sin, just as

choices.english: the Father being and existing perfect
choices.why: ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα both modify Πατέρα only; the Son and Spirit are described only with ὑφεστῶτα/ὑφεστηκός, not with ὄντα.
rejected: the Father perfect in being and person, the Son perfect in person

choices.english: I pray that you may be well in the Lord
choices.why: ἐν Κυρίῳ is present in Carterius's closing as in the others; the phrase is a standard epistolary closing.
rejected: I pray that you may be well

choices.why: The glossary specifies document for πιττάκιον, referring to the rumored Sardican document.

pass_b_english: Eusebius also subscribed to these things in Latin, and this is the translation: “I, Eusebius, bishop, with the precision that is yours, which was agreed upon by both parties as they composed it together concerning the persons, have also myself assented. Moreover, concerning the incarnation of our Savior, I have also given my assurance according to the style of the letter: that the Son of God also became man, taking up all things without sin, such as our old humanity was constituted. And since it is said abroad that the Sardican document, to avoid seeming to set forth anything beyond the faith at Nicaea, should be set aside, I also assent, that the Nicene faith not seem to be excluded by this, and that the document is not to be brought forward. I pray that you may be well in the Lord.”
I, Asterius, concur with what has been written above, and I pray that you may be well in the Lord.

And after this tome was sent from Alexandria, signed in this way by those mentioned above, after these things they themselves also subscribed: “I, Paulinus, think thus, as I received from the Fathers: the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, being and subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, being and subsisting. Therefore I also accept the interpretation written above concerning the three persons and the one person, that is, being, and those who think thus. For it is pious to think and confess the Holy Trinity in one divinity. And concerning the incarnation of the Word of the Father that took place for our sake, I think thus, as it is written: according to John, the Word became flesh (John 1:14). Not according to the most impious ones who say that he underwent change, but that he became man for our sake, born of the holy Virgin Mary and the Holy Spirit. For the Savior did not have a body without soul, without feeling, or without mind. For it was not possible, when the Lord became man for our sake, that his body should be without mind. Therefore I condemn those who reject the faith confessed at Nicaea and do not say that the Son is from the being of the Father and same in being with the Father. I condemn those who say that the Holy Spirit is a creature made through the Son. And further I condemn Sabellius and Photinus and every heresy, standing with the faith of Nicaea and with all those written above. I pray that you may be well in the Lord. I, Carterius.”

problems.quote: I also assent that it should not be brought forward
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἐγὼ συγκατατίθεμαι, ἵνα μὴ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστις διὰ τούτου ἐκκλείεσθαι δόξῃ, μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον
problems.why: The Greek says 'I assent that the Nicene faith should not seem to be excluded by it, nor that it should be brought forward.' English makes Eusebius assent to non-production; Greek has him assent to both non-exclusion AND non-production as separate points.
problems.fix: I also assent, that the Nicene faith not seem excluded by it, nor that it be brought forward

problems.quote: the Father is perfect in being and existing, the Son is perfect and existing, and the Holy Spirit is perfect and existing
problems.source_quote: Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Πατέρα τέλειον καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Υἱὸν τέλειον, καὶ ὑφεστηκὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τέλειον
problems.why: The Greek has 'Being and subsisting Father perfect, and subsisting Son perfect, and subsisting Holy Spirit perfect'—each is 'perfect' but the participles modify each person differently. English 'perfect in being and existing' only describes the Father, losing the parallel structure.
problems.fix: the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, subsisting

problems.quote: taking up all things without sin, just as our old humanity was constituted
problems.source_quote: ἀναλαβὼν πάντα ἄνευ ἁμαρτίας, οἷος ὁ παλαιὸς ἡμῶν ἄνθρωπος συνέστηκε
problems.why: πάντα means 'all things' (the whole human nature), but 'just as' renders οἷος as comparison; it means 'such as' — the same kind of humanity.
problems.fix: taking up all things without sin, such as our old humanity was constituted
problems.ruling: οἷος means 'such as/what kind' not 'just as'; comparison misrepresents Eusebius's point about Christ's full humanity.

problems.quote: according to the exactness of your investigation
problems.why: ἀκρίβεια means exactness/precision, but ὑμῶν is 'your'—the phrase refers to the exactness of the agreement itself, not an investigation. 'Your investigation' misrepresents the process.
problems.fix: according to the precision of your agreement
problems.ruling: ὑμῶν modifies ἀκρίβειαν; no 'investigation' in Greek. 'Your exactness' refers to the agreed-upon precision, not a process.

problems.quote: exists for the purpose of seeming to set forth a faith other than
problems.source_quote: ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν δοκεῖν ἐκτίθεσθαι
problems.why: ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ...δοκεῖν means 'for the sake of not seeming to set forth alongside/beyond the Nicene faith', not 'for the purpose of seeming to set forth other than'. The μὴ negates δοκεῖν, flipping the meaning.
problems.fix: exists so as not to seem to set forth beyond the faith of Nicaea
problems.ruling: μὴ negates δοκεῖν: 'lest it seem to set forth beyond Nicene faith.' English 'for the purpose of seeming' flips the meaning.

problems.quote: I also accept the interpretation written above concerning the three persons and the one person, or being
problems.source_quote: ἀποδέχομαι τὴν προγεγραμμένην ἑρμηνείαν περὶ τῶν τριῶν ὑποστάσεων, καὶ τῆς μιᾶς ὑποστάσεως, ἤτοι οὐσίας
problems.why: The Greek says 'the one person, that is, being'—ἤτοι means 'that is', identifying the one ὑπόστασις as οὐσία. English 'or being' makes it ambiguous whether these are alternatives, losing the explanatory force.
problems.fix: the one person, that is, being
problems.ruling: ἤτοι means 'that is', equating ὑπόστασις with οὐσία. 'Or being' presents them as alternatives, losing the explanatory identification.

problems.quote: following the faith of Nicaea and all that has been written above
problems.source_quote: στοιχῶν τῇ πίστει τῇ κατὰ Νίκαιαν, καὶ πᾶσι τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις
problems.why: στοιχῶν means 'standing in line with/aligning myself with', not 'following'. More critically, πᾶσι τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις is 'with all those who have been written above' (the persons), not 'all that has been written above' (the contents).
problems.fix: standing with the faith of Nicaea and with all those written above
problems.ruling: πᾶσι τοῖς προγεγραμμένοις is dative plural persons 'with all those written above', not neuter 'all that was written.' Misleads reader.

problems.source_quote: ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν δοκεῖν ἐκτίθεσθαι
problems.why: Greek says 'so as not to seem to be set forth contrary to/beside the faith at Nicaea', not 'beyond the faith of Nicaea the faith of Nicaea'.
problems.fix: so as not to seem to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea

problems.quote: I also assent, that the Nicene faith not seem excluded by it, nor that it be brought forward, lest the faith of Nicaea seem to be excluded by it
problems.source_quote: καὶ ἐγὼ συγκατατίθεμαι, ἵνα μὴ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστις διὰ τούτου ἐκκλείεσθαι δόξῃ, μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον
problems.why: English adds a repeated clause 'lest the faith of Nicaea seem to be excluded by it' not in the Greek.
problems.fix: I also assent, that the Nicene faith not seem excluded by it, nor that it be brought forward.

problems.quote: the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, subsisting
problems.source_quote: Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Πατέρα τέλειον καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Υἱὸν τέλειον, καὶ ὑφεστηκὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τέλειον
problems.why: Greek has 'being and subsisting' for Father, 'subsisting' for Son, 'subsisting' for Spirit; English misplaces 'being' and drops participles' agreement.
problems.fix: the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, subsisting
problems.ruling: Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα modifies Πατέρα; English attaches 'being and subsisting' to Father but drops ὄντα for Son and Spirit, losing asymmetry.

fixed: Corrected 'so as not to seem to set forth beyond the faith of Nicaea the faith of Nicaea' to 'so as not to seem to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea' (source: ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν δοκεῖν ἐκτίθεσθαι).
Removed the repeated clause 'lest the faith of Nicaea seem to be excluded by it' (source: ἵνα μὴ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστις διὰ τούτου ἐκκλείεσθαι δόξῃ, μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον).

Left 'the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, subsisting' unchanged; it already matches the Greek participles (Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Πατέρα τέλειον καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Υἱὸν τέλειον, καὶ ὑφεστηκὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τέλειον).

problems.quote: according to the precision of your agreement
problems.why: ὑμῶν is 'of you' plural, not 'your agreement'; ἀκρίβειαν means 'precision/accuracy', but the phrase modifies Eusebius's own action, not a 'your agreement'
problems.fix: with the precision that is yours

problems.quote: the document of Sardica exists so as not to seem to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea
problems.source_quote: τὸ τῆς Σαρδικῆς πιττάκιον ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ παρὰ τὴν ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστιν δοκεῖν ἐκτίθεσθαι
problems.why: ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ...δοκεῖν means 'for the sake of not seeming', not 'exists so as not to seem'; the document's purpose is to avoid seeming contrary to Nicaea
problems.fix: the Sardican document, for the sake of not seeming to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea

problems.quote: that the Nicene faith not seem excluded by it, nor that it be brought forward
problems.source_quote: ἵνα μὴ ἡ ἐν Νικαίᾳ πίστις διὰ τούτου ἐκκλείεσθαι δόξῃ, μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον
problems.why: μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον is 'nor that it should be produced/brought forward' as a separate clause, but 'it' ambiguously refers to the document, not the faith; and 'excluded' for ἐκκλείεσθαι is weak
problems.fix: that the Nicene faith not seem to be excluded by this, nor that the document be brought forward

problems.quote: the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, subsisting
problems.source_quote: Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Πατέρα τέλειον καὶ ὑφεστῶτα Υἱὸν τέλειον, καὶ ὑφεστηκὸς τὸ Πνεῦμα τὸ ἅγιον τέλειον
problems.why: The Greek has 'Father perfect, being and subsisting; Son perfect, subsisting; Holy Spirit perfect, subsisting'—the English breaks the parallel structure and obscures that each person is described with the same predicates
problems.fix: the Father perfect, being and subsisting; the Son perfect, being and subsisting; and the Holy Spirit perfect, being and subsisting

fixed: Corrected 'according to the precision of your agreement' to 'with the precision that is yours' to reflect that ὑμῶν is a genitive of possession modifying Eusebius's own action, not 'your agreement'.

Corrected 'the document of Sardica exists so as not to seem to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea' to 'the Sardican document, for the sake of not seeming to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea' to reflect ἕνεκεν τοῦ μὴ...δοκεῖν as 'for the sake of not seeming', not 'exists so as not to seem'.

Corrected 'that the Nicene faith not seem excluded by it, nor that it be brought forward' to 'that the Nicene faith not seem to be excluded by this, nor that the document be brought forward' to clarify that 'it' refers to the document, not the faith, and to render μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον as a separate clause about the document.
Corrected the parallel structure in Paulinus's confession to include 'being and subsisting' for each person, matching the Greek Ὄντα καὶ ὑφεστῶτα...καὶ ὑφεστῶτα...καὶ ὑφεστηκὸς.

fixed.quote: for the sake of not seeming to be set forth contrary to the faith at Nicaea, I also assent
fixed.fix: to avoid seeming to set forth anything beyond the faith at Nicaea, should be set aside, I also assent
fixed.note: The English breaks off mid-sentence after 'the Sardican document,' and misses that ἔξωθεν λέγεται means the document is being set aside so as not to seem to go beyond Nicaea; this fix repairs the sentence.

fixed.quote: nor that the document be brought forward
fixed.fix: and that the document is not to be brought forward
fixed.note: Reading 'I also assent… nor that the document be brought forward' leaves it unclear whether Eusebius agrees to its use, but μήτε εἶναι προκομιστέον plainly says it must not be produced.
